chunks: (Remember) Ishmael, Edris and Dhu'l-Kifl. They were men of fortitude,

key_terms.إِدْرِيسَ: Edris (Enoch), a prophet known for wisdom
key_terms.الصَّابِرِينَ: The patient ones, those who exhibited steadfastness
key_terms.ذَا الْكِفْلِ: Dhu'l-Kifl, a title meaning 'of the portion/double portion'

ai.seo_question: Who are Ishmael, Edris, and Dhu'l-Kifl in the Quran?
ai.summary: In Shia tradition, this verse from Surah Al-Anbiya is often cited to emphasize the virtue of sabr (patience) as a defining characteristic of the Prophets, linking their spiritual endurance to their moral authority. While classical exegetes like Al-Tabarsi and Al-Qummi discuss the identities of Edris and Dhu'l-Kifl, the verse's primary theological weight lies in presenting them as models of constancy for the faithful. This highlights the continuity of divine guidance and the shared ethical foundation among the chosen messengers.
